findings.where: article section 'What This Visual Language Is Actually Saying', 1440 tiles 03-05
findings.evidence:
The five numbered points ('1. Craft and intention.' ... '5. Rebellion against algorithmic homogenization.') are

(p:nth-of-type(12), p:nth-of-type(20)), not h3s or a list; they look like subheads but are not in the heading outline.
findings.after:
1. Craft and intention.

(or an
    whose items start with the bold lead).
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: visual subheads must be marked up so screen-reader users can navigate by them.

findings.evidence: Three links named 'Read story →' each go to a different article; the card titles are separate links. Out of context the links list shows three identical 'Read story → ' entries with the arrow read as 'right arrow'.
findings.after: Make the whole card one link named by the title, or add OpenAI DevDay: 25 releases and aria-hidden on the arrow.

findings.where: CTA band portrait and footer CTA images
findings.evidence: The Stef Nimmegeers portrait in the CTA band has alt="" (acceptable beside the visible name), but the same WhatsApp phone alt "Top portion of a smartphone screen showing a WhatsApp chat with Nimble..." is reused on SnippetFooter.png and 'Steps Container.png', which show different things.
findings.before: Same alt on three different images
findings.after: Write an alt per image, or alt="" where the image repeats the adjacent text.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content: alt must describe the image it is on.

findings.evidence: Emoji close several paragraphs ('Figma template. 😉', 'processing speed. 🤝🏻', 'what it means to care. 🫶🏻'); screen readers announce 'handshake medium-light skin tone' mid-reading.
findings.after: Wrap in <span role="img" aria-label=""> or aria-hidden="true" if decorative.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content (decorative glyphs should be hidden).

strengths: Article images have long, descriptive alts that carry what the image shows (mood board, AI workflow canvas, NimbleFest hero with 'Ghent, Bar Bricolage' and countdown).
Skip link ('skip to main content') is the first focusable; focus order follows the page top to bottom; nav dropdown toggles have role=button.
Body text is near-black on white at 18px with a readable measure.
not_investigated: Sweep fallback_face Floor hits ('declared Suisseintl but Suisse Int'l drew the text') look like a naming mismatch for the same family, not a missing font: disputed: same face rendered under a different family name.
Keyboard operation of the Industries/Technologies mega-menu dropdowns (live session needed).
